definition: A contract structure where the developer acts purely as a paid contractor to produce oil and gas for a fee, without taking ownership of the crude oil produced.
core_idea: Under a service contract the developer is compensated as a fee-for-service provider rather than as a profit-or-loss stakeholder in the extracted fuel itself.
key_points: Developer is paid a fee to produce oil and gas.
Developer does not take ownership of the crude oil produced.
relationships: Represents the lowest-risk-for-developer end of the E&P contract spectrum, contrasted with tax and royalty and production sharing where the developer/owner take on production or price risk.
